Commentary.Commentary: Onto the next one - Right then, that is it from this first warm-up game, where Scotland Women brushed aside the Netherlands Women with ease. However, don’t go anywhere as the action does not stop here in Derby. We have two Asian giants, Pakistan Women and Sri Lanka Women, going up against each other shortly. You can just switch tabs to enjoy all the coverage of that game.

The victorious skipper of Scotland Women - Kathryn Bryce says that the bowling was exceptional, and so was the fielding from the team. Adds that the partnership between Priyanaz Chatterji and Pippa Sproul was good. Mentions that the team is in good shape and the fans are buzzing for the marquee event.

The captain of Netherlands Women - Babette de Leede says bowling was not good enough, and the fielding was weak. Adds that it’s been a busy couple of days, so they will take some rest and come back stronger. Mentions that playing in the stadium feels special and close to the World Cup. Says that they have worked very hard to be here. They have got another week to get things right and will work on areas before coming back stronger.
Let's hear from the two captains now...

Clinical bowling display - Scotland Women controlled proceedings with the ball. It was young Gabriella Fontenla who struck twice in her first two overs, setting the tone, while Olivia Bell followed up with another. They never let the Dutch get going, picking up wickets at regular intervals while also keeping the runs in check. Katherine Fraser was the best bowler with a three-wicket haul, while Abtaha Maqsood took a couple and Chloe Abel also chipped in with one. A run-out on the last ball of the game wrapped things up, sealing a perfect day for them.

Strong finish puts Scotland in control - Earlier in the game, Scotland Women posted a good total on the board, courtesy of a couple of 30s from Darcey Carter and skipper Kathryn Bryce. Priyanaz Chatterji provided the late momentum with a quick 32 off 20, alongside Pippa Sproul, who also struck a few lusty blows. Silver Siegers was the pick of the bowlers for Netherlands Women with a couple of wickets, while Iris, Iris Zwilling and Myrthe van den Raad chipped in with one each, but they just could not maintain control over the scoring rate.

Powerplay damage proves costly for the Dutch - Well, there is not much to talk about Netherlands Women batting. They were reduced to 21/3 in the Powerplay, effectively taking them out of the game. Phebe Molkenboer and Robine Rijke offered some resistance with a 30-run stand, but perished while trying to up the ante. Frederique Overdijk then scored valuable runs alongside Caroline de Lange, staying unbeaten on 28, which was never going to be enough in this chase, but helped salvage some pride by taking them to three figures.

Scotland Women too strong for Netherlands - A comprehensive victory for Scotland Women, and after beating the Dutch a couple of times in the recent tri-series, they have got the better of them again. To be fair, it was a dominant performance from them. Although this is only a warm-up, the heavy defeat will force the Netherlands to rethink a few things going into their maiden T20 World Cup.

OUT! RUN OUT TO END THE GAME! Flighted full on the leg pole. Silver Siegers shuffles and sweeps it toward the long leg region. She wants another couple, but the throw comes at the keeper's end from Carter, and Sarah Bryce does the rest. Netherlands Women are dismissed for 105. Scotland Women win by 58 runs.
